pages.title: Kalkulator wynagrodzeń: na zmierzonych danych
pages.description: Kalkulator wynagrodzeń od Livdar, liczony na danych Eurostat, a nie na zgłoszeniach użytkowników, z wszystkimi danymi wejściowymi i założeniami na wierzchu.
paragraphs: Obliczenia opierają się tutaj na danych Eurostat. Dane wejściowe są widoczne, założenia są spisane, a wynik jest przedziałem zamiast jednej liczby wszędzie tam, gdzie dane źródłowe pozwalają tylko na przedział.

Pytanie brzmi, ile daje praca w jednym kraju wobec drugiego, mierzone tą samą definicją po obu stronach. Opublikowana seria obejmuje osobę samotną o przeciętnym wynagrodzeniu, przed potrąceniami i po nich, i tylko takie porównanie wytrzymuje przekroczenie granicy: kwota brutto jest u sąsiada opodatkowana inaczej, a dwie kwoty brutto z dwóch systemów podatkowych to nie dwa razy ta sama liczba. Czego narzędzie nie potrafi, to wycenić konkretnego stanowiska. Zawód, branża, staż i pracodawca ruszają płacę mocniej niż kraj, a nic z tego nie siedzi w tej serii.
Przykład na liczbach: Austria w roku 2025. Z 5219 euro brutto miesięcznie po podatkach i składkach zostaje 3529 euro, czyli różnica 32,4 procent.
Obejmuje 35 krajów, czyli dokładnie tyle, ile mierzy źródło, i ani jednego więcej.

Liczby stojące za tym narzędziem opisują rok 2025 i zmieniają się wtedy, gdy publikuje je Eurostat, a nie wtedy, gdy ktoś edytuje tę stronę. Dlatego rok stoi obok każdej wartości, a nie w przypisie: narzędzie z rocznymi danymi, które o tym mówi, jest bardziej użyteczne niż takie, które wygląda na aktualne, a nie jest.

faq.q: Skąd pochodzą liczby?
faq.a: Obliczenia opierają się na danych Eurostat. Każda użyta wartość niesie ze sobą instytucję, która ją opublikowała, i rok, którego dotyczy.

faq.q: Czy wynik to wycena?
faq.a: Nie. To szacunek z opublikowanych statystyk, i jest napisane, z których i za który rok. Wiążące jest dopiero to, co poda ten, kto wystawi rachunek.

pages.title: Salary calculator: built on measured data
pages.description: Salary calculator from Livdar, computed against Eurostat rather than crowd submitted figures, with every input and assumption shown.
paragraphs: Salary calculator here is computed against Eurostat. The inputs are shown, the assumptions are written down, and the result is a range rather than a single number wherever the underlying data supports only a range.

The question here is what a job pays in one country against another, measured on the same definition in both. The published series covers a single person on the average wage, before and after tax, which is the only comparison that holds across borders: a headline salary in one country is taxed differently in the next, and two gross figures from two tax systems are not the same number twice. What it cannot do is price a particular job. Occupation, sector, seniority and employer all move pay more than the country does, and none of them is in this series.
Worked example: Austria in 2025. Gross pay of 5,219 euro a month leaves 3,529 euro after tax and contributions, a gap of 32.4 percent.
It covers 35 countries, which is exactly the set the source measures and no more.

The figures behind this tool describe 2025 and they change when Eurostat publishes, not when this page is edited. That is why the year appears next to every value rather than in the small print: a tool whose data is a year old and says so is more useful than one that looks current and is not.

faq.q: Where do the numbers come from?
faq.a: Salary calculator computes against Eurostat. Every figure it uses carries the institution that published it and the year it describes.

faq.q: Is the result a quote?
faq.a: No. It is an estimate from published statistics, and it says which statistics and for which year. Anything binding has to come from whoever is going to charge you.

pages.title: Gehaltsrechner: auf gemessenen Daten
pages.description: Gehaltsrechner von Livdar, gerechnet auf Eurostat statt auf Nutzerangaben, mit allen Eingaben und Annahmen offen.
paragraphs: Gehaltsrechner rechnet hier auf Eurostat. Die Eingaben stehen offen, die Annahmen sind aufgeschrieben, und das Ergebnis ist eine Spanne statt einer einzelnen Zahl, wo die zugrunde liegenden Daten nur eine Spanne hergeben.

Die Frage ist, was eine Arbeit in einem Land im Vergleich zu einem anderen einbringt, gemessen nach derselben Definition. Die veröffentlichte Reihe erfasst eine alleinstehende Person mit Durchschnittsverdienst, vor und nach Abzügen, und nur dieser Vergleich hält über Grenzen hinweg: ein Bruttogehalt wird im Nachbarland anders besteuert, zwei Bruttozahlen aus zwei Steuersystemen sind nicht zweimal dieselbe Zahl. Was der Rechner nicht kann, ist eine bestimmte Stelle zu bewerten. Beruf, Branche, Erfahrung und Arbeitgeber bewegen das Gehalt stärker als das Land, und nichts davon steckt in dieser Reihe.
Rechenbeispiel: Österreich im Jahr 2025. Von 5.219 Euro brutto im Monat bleiben nach Steuern und Beiträgen 3.529 Euro, eine Differenz von 32,4 Prozent.
Erfasst werden 35 Länder, genau der Bestand der Quelle und kein Land mehr.

Die Werte hinter diesem Rechner beschreiben das Jahr 2025 und ändern sich, wenn Eurostat neu veröffentlicht, nicht wenn diese Seite bearbeitet wird. Deshalb steht das Jahr neben jedem Wert und nicht im Kleingedruckten: ein Rechner, dessen Daten ein Jahr alt sind und der das sagt, ist nützlicher als einer, der aktuell aussieht und es nicht ist.

faq.q: Woher kommen die Zahlen?
faq.a: Gehaltsrechner rechnet auf Eurostat. Jeder verwendete Wert nennt die Institution, die ihn veröffentlicht hat, und das Jahr, das er beschreibt.

faq.q: Ist das Ergebnis ein Angebot?
faq.a: Nein. Es ist eine Schätzung aus veröffentlichten Statistiken, und sie nennt welche und für welches Jahr. Verbindlich wird es erst bei dem, der Ihnen etwas berechnet.

sources.licence: see the source registry
sources.attribution: Eurostat

pages.title: 給与計算：測定データにもとづく
pages.description: Livdar の給与計算。利用者の投稿ではなく Eurostat をもとに計算し、入力と前提をすべて表に出す。

facts.label: 入力する項目
facts.value: 職種, 都市, 経験年数

paragraphs: ここでの計算は Eurostat にもとづく。入力は表に出し、前提は文章で書き、元データが幅しか支えられないところでは結果も一つの数ではなく幅で示す。

問いは、ある国の仕事が別の国と比べていくらになるかであり、両方を同じ定義で測っている。公表されている系列が扱うのは平均賃金の単身者で、控除の前と後の両方。国境をまたいでも成り立つ比較はこれだけである。総支給は隣の国では別の課税を受けるので、二つの税制から出た二つの総支給額は同じ数字が二度あるわけではない。この計算ができないのは、特定の求人を値付けすることである。職種、業種、経験、雇い主のほうが国よりも給与を動かすが、そのどれもこの系列には入っていない。
計算例：2025年のオーストリア。月の総支給 5,219 ユーロから、税と社会保険料を引いて手取りは 3,529 ユーロ。差は 32.4 パーセントになる。
対象は 35 か国。出典が測定している範囲とちょうど同じで、それ以上には広げない。
この計算の裏にある数値は 2025年を表しており、Eurostat が新しく公表したときに変わる。このページを書き直したときではない。だから年は小さな注記ではなく値の横に置いている。データが一年前でもそう書いてある道具のほうが、新しそうに見えて実はそうでない道具より役に立つ。

faq.q: 数値の出どころはどこですか。
faq.a: 計算は Eurostat にもとづきます。使う値にはすべて、公表した機関と対象年が付いています。

faq.q: 結果は見積もりですか。
faq.a: いいえ。公表された統計からの推計で、どの統計の何年分かを明記しています。拘束力があるのは、実際に請求する相手が出す数字です。

pages.title: Cost of living comparison: built on measured data
pages.description: Cost of living comparison from Livdar, computed against Eurostat + World Bank rather than crowd submitted figures, with every input and assumption shown.
paragraphs: Cost of living comparison here is computed against Eurostat + World Bank. The inputs are shown, the assumptions are written down, and the result is a range rather than a single number wherever the underlying data supports only a range.

The question here is which of two places is dearer, and by how much. It is answered by putting the same standard basket in both and reading the gap, which is why the pair has to be measured on one scale: comparing a country on the European index with a country on the World Bank ratio produces a number, and the number means nothing. The comparison refuses that pairing instead of converting between the two, because the conversion would be an invention. It also cannot tell you whether you would be better off, which depends on your income and not on the basket.
Worked example: Switzerland against Türkiye. The same standard basket costs about 294 percent more in the first, on the 2024 figures.
It covers 199 countries, which is exactly the set the source measures and no more.

The figures behind this tool describe 2024 and they change when Eurostat + World Bank publishes, not when this page is edited. That is why the year appears next to every value rather than in the small print: a tool whose data is a year old and says so is more useful than one that looks current and is not.

faq.a: Cost of living comparison computes against Eurostat + World Bank. Every figure it uses carries the institution that published it and the year it describes.

pages.title: Calculadora de salario: sobre dados medidos
pages.description: Calculadora de salario da Livdar, calculado sobre Eurostat e não sobre valores enviados por utilizadores, com todas as entradas e pressupostos à vista.
paragraphs: O cálculo assenta aqui em Eurostat. As entradas estão à vista, os pressupostos estão escritos e o resultado é um intervalo em vez de um número único sempre que os dados de base só aguentem um intervalo.

A pergunta é quanto rende um trabalho num país face a outro, medido pela mesma definição dos dois lados. A série publicada cobre uma pessoa sozinha com salário médio, antes e depois de impostos, e é a única comparação que aguenta de fronteira para fronteira: um bruto não é tributado da mesma maneira no país ao lado, e dois valores brutos de dois sistemas fiscais não são duas vezes o mesmo número. O que não consegue fazer é pôr preço a um posto concreto. Profissão, setor, antiguidade e empregador mexem no ordenado mais do que o país, e nada disso está nesta série.
Exemplo com números: a Áustria em 2025. De 5.219 euros brutos por mês sobram 3.529 euros depois de impostos e contribuições, uma distância de 32,4 por cento.
Cobre 35 países, exatamente os que a fonte mede e nem um a mais.

Os números por trás desta ferramenta descrevem 2025 e mudam quando Eurostat publica, não quando esta página é editada. É por isso que o ano aparece ao lado de cada valor e não nas letras pequenas: uma ferramenta com dados de há um ano que o diz é mais útil do que outra que parece atual e não está.

faq.q: De onde vêm os números?
faq.a: O cálculo assenta em Eurostat. Cada valor usado traz a instituição que o publicou e o ano que descreve.

faq.q: O resultado é um orçamento?
faq.a: Não. É uma estimativa a partir de estatísticas publicadas, e diz quais e de que ano. O que compromete vem de quem lhe vai cobrar.

pages.title: Cost of living calculator: built on measured data
pages.description: Cost of living calculator from Livdar, computed against Eurostat + World Bank rather than crowd submitted figures, with every input and assumption shown.
paragraphs: Cost of living calculator here is computed against Eurostat + World Bank. The inputs are shown, the assumptions are written down, and the result is a range rather than a single number wherever the underlying data supports only a range.

The question here is what one place costs for one household, rather than how two places compare. That makes it the harder of the two calculators to answer honestly, because a household is not a standard basket: the published index weights spending the way the average household spends it, and almost nobody is the average household. The calculator therefore shows the twelve categories separately and lets the reader weight them, instead of producing a single monthly figure that would be precise and wrong for everyone who reads it.
Worked example: Switzerland against Türkiye. The same standard basket costs about 294 percent more in the first, on the 2024 figures.
It covers 199 countries, which is exactly the set the source measures and no more.

The figures behind this tool describe 2024 and they change when Eurostat + World Bank publishes, not when this page is edited. That is why the year appears next to every value rather than in the small print: a tool whose data is a year old and says so is more useful than one that looks current and is not.

pages.title: Where should I live: built on measured data
pages.description: Where should I live from Livdar, computed against Eurostat + World Bank + Eurostat rather than crowd submitted figures, with every input and assumption shown.

facts.label: What it asks for
facts.value: budget, climate, language, work situation, priorities

paragraphs: Where should I live here is computed against Eurostat + World Bank + Eurostat. The inputs are shown, the assumptions are written down, and the result is a range rather than a single number wherever the underlying data supports only a range.

The question here is the vaguest one anybody asks and the hardest to answer without flattering the reader. Most quizzes of this shape have no data behind the answer at all: they ask five questions about your personality and name a city. This one filters on measured things, price level and pay and the presence of a source at all, and it returns fewer places than a quiz would because it will not name a country it has no figures for. It cannot weigh what actually decides these moves, which is usually a person or a job rather than a number.

Worked example: of 39 countries in the store, 24 come in under the European Union average price level. That is the kind of filter the matcher applies, and it never returns a country the source does not cover.
It covers 199 countries, which is exactly the set the source measures and no more.

The figures behind this tool describe 2024 and they change when Eurostat + World Bank + Eurostat publishes, not when this page is edited. That is why the year appears next to every value rather than in the small print: a tool whose data is a year old and says so is more useful than one that looks current and is not.

paragraphs: Where should I live here is computed against Eurostat + World Bank + Eurostat. The inputs are shown, the assumptions are written down, and the result is a range rather than a single number wherever the underlying data supports only a range.

The question here is the vaguest one anybody asks and the hardest to answer without flattering the reader. Most quizzes of this shape have no data behind the answer at all: they ask five questions about your personality and name a city. This one filters on measured things, price level and pay and the presence of a source at all, and it returns fewer places than a quiz would because it will not name a country it has no figures for. It cannot weigh what actually decides these moves, which is usually a person or a job rather than a number.

Worked example: of 39 countries in the store, 24 come in under the European Union average price level. That is the kind of filter the matcher applies, and it never returns a country the source does not cover.
It covers 199 countries, which is exactly the set the source measures and no more.

The figures behind this tool describe 2024 and they change when Eurostat + World Bank + Eurostat publishes, not when this page is edited. That is why the year appears next to every value rather than in the small print: a tool whose data is a year old and says so is more useful than one that looks current and is not.

pages.title: Custo de vida em Portugal: o que o nível de preços diz de facto
pages.description: Portugal: quanto custa viver lá, medido e não estimado: o nível de preços é de 85 para 2024, com a divisão por categorias e a fonte de cada número.

facts.label: Tudo o que uma família compra

paragraphs: Portugal tem um nível de preços de 85 quando a média da União Europeia vale 100, medido para 2024. Um cabaz de consumo custa lá cerca de 15 por cento a menos do que o mesmo cabaz no conjunto da União.
Para este país são publicadas doze categorias de despesa, por isso a divisão abaixo é medida e não deduzida do número global.
Dentro do cabaz a distância é maior do que o número global sugere. A categoria mais cara é Telefone e internet, com 115,6, e a mais barata Educação, com 72.
Portugal: os preços subiram 2,2 por cento no ano até 2024, pelo que os números acima já terão andado um pouco desde que foram recolhidos.
Portugal ocupa a posição 17 entre os 39 países que esta fonte mede na mesma escala, o que o coloca na metade mais barata desse grupo.
Na mesma escala fica entre Grécia com 83 e Japão com 89, que é a companhia real por trás de um lugar 17 em 39.
Diretamente comparável com outros 38 países medidos na mesma escala.

Um nível de preços não é um orçamento. Compara um cabaz padronizado entre países e não sabe nada do que ganha, da distância entre a capital e uma vila, nem do que paga de renda quem acaba de chegar face a quem já lá mora há anos. Leia-o como ponto de partida para comparar e não como um número com que fazer planos.

pages.title: Calcolo stipendio: su dati misurati
pages.description: Calcolo stipendio di Livdar, calcolato su Eurostat e non su segnalazioni degli utenti, con tutti gli ingressi e le ipotesi in chiaro.
paragraphs: Il calcolo qui si appoggia a Eurostat. Gli ingressi sono in chiaro, le ipotesi sono scritte e il risultato è un intervallo invece di un numero secco ovunque i dati di partenza reggano solo un intervallo.

La domanda è quanto rende un lavoro in un paese rispetto a un altro, misurato con la stessa definizione da entrambe le parti. La serie pubblicata copre una persona sola con retribuzione media, prima e dopo il prelievo, ed è l'unico confronto che regge fra un paese e l'altro: un lordo non viene tassato allo stesso modo oltre confine, e due importi lordi di due sistemi fiscali non sono due volte lo stesso numero. Quello che lo strumento non può fare è valutare un posto preciso. Mestiere, settore, anzianità e datore di lavoro spostano la retribuzione più del paese, e niente di tutto questo sta in questa serie.
Esempio con i numeri: l'Austria nel 2025. Da 5219 euro lordi al mese restano 3529 euro dopo imposte e contributi, una distanza del 32,4 per cento.
Copre 35 paesi, esattamente quelli che la fonte misura e non uno di più.

I numeri dietro questo strumento descrivono il 2025 e cambiano quando pubblica Eurostat, non quando si modifica questa pagina. Per questo l'anno sta accanto a ogni valore e non in fondo: uno strumento con dati vecchi di un anno che lo dichiara è più utile di uno che sembra aggiornato e non lo è.

faq.q: Da dove vengono i numeri?
faq.a: Il calcolo si appoggia a Eurostat. Ogni valore usato porta con sé l'istituzione che lo ha pubblicato e l'anno che descrive.

faq.q: Il risultato è un preventivo?
faq.a: No. È una stima da statistiche pubblicate, e dice quali e di che anno. Quello che impegna arriva da chi poi ti fattura.

pages.description: Moving cost calculator from Livdar, computed against Livdar rather than crowd submitted figures, with every input and assumption shown.

facts.label: What it asks for
facts.value: origin city, destination city, home size, date

paragraphs: Moving cost calculator here is computed against Livdar. The inputs are shown, the assumptions are written down, and the result is a range rather than a single number wherever the underlying data supports only a range.

The question here is what it costs to move a household from one place to another, and it is the one tool on this site with no statistical office behind it, because no statistical office publishes removal prices. The model is Livdar's own: volume, distance, crew hours, packing, insurance and the handling that crossing a border adds. Volume beyond one vehicle becomes a second trip, which is the step a linear estimate misses and the reason cheap online quotes come in low. The answer is always a range with its assumptions attached, never a single number, and it is never a quote.
Worked example: a two bedroom home moved five hundred kilometres comes out between 1,095 and 1,715 euro, and the tool says which assumptions produced each end of that range.

The method is not a secret and not a model anybody has to trust. The tool reads the published values from Livdar, applies the arithmetic the page describes, and shows the year of every value it used, so a reader who disagrees with the answer can see exactly which number they disagree with.

faq.a: Moving cost calculator computes against Livdar. Every figure it uses carries the institution that published it and the year it describes.

faq.q: Is the result a quote?
faq.a: No. It is an estimate from published statistics, and it says which statistics and for which year. Anything binding has to come from whoever is going to charge you.

pages.title: Average salary in Italy: gross, net and the minimum wage
pages.description: What Italy pays, from the official European earnings series: net pay averages 2,316 euro a month for 2025, shown next to gross pay and the statutory minimum.
paragraphs: Italy pays 3,338 euro a month on average before tax and 2,316 euro after, measured for 2025. Both figures describe a single person without children on the average wage, which is the case the source publishes.
Italy takes about 30.6 percent of a gross wage in income tax and social contributions, which is the gap between the two figures above rather than a rate anybody is charged.
Italy has no statutory minimum wage set in law. Pay floors there are set by collective agreement per sector, so there is no single national number to quote.
Italy ranks 12 of 27 countries in the series on net pay, where the middle country is at 2,106 euro a month.
That puts Italy about 10 percent above the median of these 27 countries, which is 2,106 a month.
On the same series Italy sits between Cyprus at 2,362 and Spain at 2,253, which is what a rank on its own does not tell you.

Pay only means something next to prices. The same source puts the price level in Italy at 98.1 on the index, EU average = 100 for 2024, so a wage that looks high or low against its neighbours may not be once the cost of the basket is put beside it.
An average is not a typical salary. It is pulled upward by high earners, it says nothing about any particular job, and it is worth reading next to the cost of living rather than on its own.

faq.q: Is this before or after tax?
faq.a: Both are shown. Gross is before income tax and social contributions, net is after, and the difference between them is the wedge figure on this page.

faq.q: Does this mean I would earn 2,316 euro a month in Italy?
faq.a: No. This is the average for a single person on the average wage in 2025. What any individual earns depends on the occupation, the sector, the region and the employer, none of which this series splits out.

pages.h1: Most expensive countries to live in
pages.title: Most expensive countries to live in: the measured list
pages.description: Most expensive countries to live in, ranked on one measure across 199 countries for 2025. Every figure is quoted as ratio, United States = 1 and cites the institution that published it.
paragraphs: Sudan comes top of this list at 2.15, out of 199 countries measured on the same scale for 2025. The measure is a price level quoted as ratio, United States = 1.

Expensive is not the same as unaffordable. The countries at the top of this list are mostly high wage economies with strong currencies, and a resident earning locally may be no worse off than somebody in a cheap country earning local wages there. The list answers what a visitor or a newcomer pays, which is the case where a high price level genuinely hurts, because the income has not moved with the prices.

The list sorts on one measure, the World Bank price level ratio, quoted as ratio, United States = 1, and it covers 199 of the roughly 195 countries it claims. Nothing is blended: a list that mixed two price measures on two scales would be ordering two different things and would put currency regimes at the top rather than cheap countries.
A price level is not a cost of living for a person. It compares a standard basket across countries and takes no account of what you earn, where you live inside the country, or what you actually buy.

pages.title: 物価の安い国：測定にもとづく一覧
pages.description: 物価の安い国を、2021年の 199 か国について単一の指標で並べた一覧。各数値は単位 比率、米国 = 1 で示し、公表した機関を明記する。
paragraphs: この一覧の先頭は 南スーダン で 0.06。2021年に同じ尺度で測定された 199 か国の中での順位である。指標は単位 比率、米国 = 1 の物価水準。
物価の低さは単独では現れにくい。たいていは賃金の低さと通貨の弱さを伴うので、この一覧の上位にある国は、よそからの収入を持って来る人にとって安いのであって、そこで稼ぐ人にとって必ずしも安いわけではない。同じ国の賃金の数字と並べて読むときに最も役に立ち、おすすめの一覧として読むときには何の役にも立たない。
並べ替えは単一の指標 世界銀行の物価水準比率（単位 比率、米国 = 1）だけで行い、題名が対象とする約 195 か国のうち 199 か国を収めている。混ぜることはしない。二つの尺度の物価指標を混ぜた一覧は、異なる二つのものを並べることになり、物価の安い国ではなく通貨制度を上位に押し上げてしまう。
物価水準は個人の生活費ではない。国どうしで標準化した買い物かごを比べるもので、収入も、国内のどこに住むかも、実際に何を買うかも織り込んでいない。

faq.q: 入っていない国があるのはなぜですか。
faq.a: この尺度で測定されていないからです。この指標の値を持つのは 199 か国で、別の尺度の国を足すと一覧は広がるどころか順序が壊れます。

faq.q: この数字は何を意味しますか。
faq.a: 単位 比率、米国 = 1 の物価水準です。ある国が別の国の二倍なら、同じ標準的な買い物かごにおよそ二倍かかるということです。

pages.title: Cost of living in Norway: what the price level actually says
pages.description: What Norway costs, measured rather than estimated: the price level is 134.1, recorded for 2024, with the category breakdown and the source behind every figure.
paragraphs: Norway has a price level of 134.1 where the European Union average is 100, measured for 2024. A household basket there costs about 34 percent more than the same basket across the Union.
Twelve spending categories are published for this country, so the breakdown below is measured rather than inferred from the headline.
The spread inside the basket is wider than the headline suggests. Alcohol and tobacco is the most expensive category at 205.3, and Housing, water and energy the least at 99.9.
Norway: prices rose 2.8 percent over the year to 2024, so the figures above will have drifted a little since they were recorded.
Norway is the 33 cheapest of the 39 countries this source measures on the same scale, which places it in the dearer half of that group.
On the same scale it sits between United Kingdom at 129.1 and Ireland at 141.2, which is the company that a rank of 33 out of 39 puts it in.
Directly comparable with 38 other countries measured on the same scale.

A price level is not a budget. It compares a standard basket between countries and takes no account of what you earn, of the difference between the capital and a small town, or of what a newcomer pays for rent as opposed to what a sitting tenant pays. Read it as a starting point for a comparison, not as a figure to plan around.

faq.q: Norway: is it an expensive country to live in?
faq.a: Measured against the reference this figure uses, the price level is 134.1 for 2024. That is the whole answer this page can give honestly, because a price level says what a basket costs and not what your life costs.

faq.q: What year is this figure from?
faq.a: It is the value recorded for 2024. Price level statistics are annual and always lag, so this is the most recent one published rather than a figure for today.

faq.q: Can I compare this with another country here?
faq.a: Only with countries measured on the same scale. This one is quoted as index, EU average = 100, and a country quoted on the other scale is not comparable with it without a conversion nobody has measured.

pages.description: Compare cities from Livdar, computed against Eurostat + World Bank + Eurostat rather than crowd submitted figures, with every input and assumption shown.
paragraphs: Compare cities here is computed against Eurostat + World Bank + Eurostat. The inputs are shown, the assumptions are written down, and the result is a range rather than a single number wherever the underlying data supports only a range.

The question here is how two places stand against each other across several measures at once rather than on one headline. That is the useful comparison and it is also where a tool most easily misleads, by lining up numbers that were collected differently and letting the layout imply they belong side by side. So each row says which measure it is, which year it describes and which institution published it, and a row that exists for one side and not the other stays visibly empty rather than being filled with the other side's figure.
Worked example: Switzerland against Türkiye. The same standard basket costs about 294 percent more in the first, on the 2024 figures.
It covers 199 countries, which is exactly the set the source measures and no more.

The figures behind this tool describe 2024 and they change when Eurostat + World Bank + Eurostat publishes, not when this page is edited. That is why the year appears next to every value rather than in the small print: a tool whose data is a year old and says so is more useful than one that looks current and is not.

pages.title: Calculadora de salario: sobre datos medidos
pages.description: Calculadora de salario de Livdar, calculado sobre Eurostat y no sobre datos enviados por usuarios, con todas las entradas y los supuestos a la vista.
paragraphs: El cálculo se hace aquí sobre Eurostat. Las entradas están a la vista, los supuestos están escritos y el resultado es una horquilla en lugar de un número único siempre que los datos de base solo den para una horquilla.

La pregunta es qué paga un trabajo en un país frente a otro, medido con la misma definición en ambos. La serie publicada cubre a una persona sola con salario medio, antes y después de impuestos, y esa es la única comparación que aguanta de una frontera a otra: un bruto no tributa igual en el país vecino, y dos cifras brutas de dos sistemas fiscales no son dos veces la misma cifra. Lo que no puede hacer es poner precio a un puesto concreto. Oficio, sector, antigüedad y empresa mueven el sueldo más que el país, y nada de eso está en esta serie.
Ejemplo con cifras: Austria en 2025. De 5219 euros brutos al mes quedan 3529 euros tras impuestos y cotizaciones, una distancia del 32,4 por ciento.
Cubre 35 países, exactamente los que mide la fuente y ni uno más.

Las cifras que hay detrás de esta herramienta describen 2025 y cambian cuando publica Eurostat, no cuando se edita esta página. Por eso el año aparece junto a cada valor y no en la letra pequeña: una herramienta cuyos datos tienen un año y lo dice es más útil que otra que parece actual y no lo está.

faq.q: ¿De dónde salen las cifras?
faq.a: El cálculo se apoya en Eurostat. Cada valor que usa lleva la institución que lo publicó y el año que describe.

faq.q: ¿El resultado es un presupuesto?
faq.a: No. Es una estimación a partir de estadísticas publicadas, y dice cuáles y de qué año. Lo que compromete llega de quien te vaya a cobrar.

Ejemplo con cifras: Austria en 2025. De 5219 euros brutos al mes quedan 3529 euros tras impuestos y cotizaciones, una distancia del 32,4 por ciento.
Cubre 35 países, exactamente los que mide la fuente y ni uno más.

Las cifras que hay detrás de esta herramienta describen 2025 y cambian cuando publica Eurostat, no cuando se edita esta página. Por eso el año aparece junto a cada valor y no en la letra pequeña: una herramienta cuyos datos tienen un año y lo dice es más útil que otra que parece actual y no lo está.

pages.title: Cheapest countries to live in: the measured list
pages.description: Cheapest countries to live in, ranked on one measure across 199 countries for 2021. Every figure is quoted as ratio, United States = 1 and cites the institution that published it.
paragraphs: South Sudan comes top of this list at 0.06, out of 199 countries measured on the same scale for 2021. The measure is a price level quoted as ratio, United States = 1.

A low price level rarely arrives on its own. It usually travels with lower wages and a weaker currency, so a country near the top of this list is cheap for somebody arriving with income from elsewhere and not necessarily cheap for somebody earning there. The ranking is most useful read next to the pay figures for the same country, and least useful read as a recommendation.

The list sorts on one measure, the World Bank price level ratio, quoted as ratio, United States = 1, and it covers 199 of the roughly 195 countries it claims. Nothing is blended: a list that mixed two price measures on two scales would be ordering two different things and would put currency regimes at the top rather than cheap countries.
A price level is not a cost of living for a person. It compares a standard basket across countries and takes no account of what you earn, where you live inside the country, or what you actually buy.

faq.q: Why are some countries missing?
faq.a: Because they are not measured on this scale. 199 countries carry a value for this measure, and adding a country from the other scale would break the ordering rather than extend it.

faq.q: What does the number mean?
faq.a: It is a price level quoted as ratio, United States = 1. A country at twice another country is roughly twice as expensive for the same standard basket.

pages.title: Custo de vida no Japão: o que o nível de preços diz de facto
pages.description: Japão: quanto custa viver lá, medido e não estimado: o nível de preços é de 89 para 2024, com a divisão por categorias e a fonte de cada número.

facts.label: Tudo o que uma família compra

paragraphs: O Japão tem um nível de preços de 89 quando a média da União Europeia vale 100, medido para 2024. Um cabaz de consumo custa lá cerca de 11 por cento a menos do que o mesmo cabaz no conjunto da União.
Deste país só é publicado o nível de preços global. A divisão em doze categorias existe para os estados membros da União Europeia e não para este, e aqui nada tapa esse buraco com uma estimativa.
Esta fonte não tem série anual de inflação para o Japão, pelo que daqui não se consegue dizer quanto o valor andou desde que foi recolhido.
O Japão ocupa a posição 18 entre os 39 países que esta fonte mede na mesma escala, o que o coloca na metade mais barata desse grupo.
Na mesma escala fica entre Portugal com 85 e Espanha com 90,7, que é a companhia real por trás de um lugar 18 em 39.
Diretamente comparável com outros 38 países medidos na mesma escala.

Um nível de preços não é um orçamento. Compara um cabaz padronizado entre países e não sabe nada do que ganha, da distância entre a capital e uma vila, nem do que paga de renda quem acaba de chegar face a quem já lá mora há anos. Leia-o como ponto de partida para comparar e não como um número com que fazer planos.

pages.title: Average salary in France: gross, net and the minimum wage
pages.description: What France pays, from the official European earnings series: net pay averages 2,696 euro a month for 2025, shown next to gross pay and the statutory minimum.
paragraphs: France pays 3,700 euro a month on average before tax and 2,696 euro after, measured for 2025. Both figures describe a single person without children on the average wage, which is the case the source publishes.
France takes about 27.1 percent of a gross wage in income tax and social contributions, which is the gap between the two figures above rather than a rate anybody is charged.
The statutory minimum wage is 1,867 euro a month for 2026.
France ranks 10 of 27 countries in the series on net pay, where the middle country is at 2,106 euro a month.
That puts France about 28 percent above the median of these 27 countries, which is 2,106 a month.
On the same series France sits between Belgium at 3,035 and Cyprus at 2,362, which is what a rank on its own does not tell you.

Pay only means something next to prices. The same source puts the price level in France at 107.9 on the index, EU average = 100 for 2024, so a wage that looks high or low against its neighbours may not be once the cost of the basket is put beside it.
An average is not a typical salary. It is pulled upward by high earners, it says nothing about any particular job, and it is worth reading next to the cost of living rather than on its own.

faq.q: Is this before or after tax?
faq.a: Both are shown. Gross is before income tax and social contributions, net is after, and the difference between them is the wedge figure on this page.

faq.q: Does this mean I would earn 2,696 euro a month in France?
faq.a: No. This is the average for a single person on the average wage in 2025. What any individual earns depends on the occupation, the sector, the region and the employer, none of which this series splits out.

pages.title: Cout demenagement : sur des données mesurées
pages.description: Cout demenagement de Livdar, calculé sur Livdar plutôt que sur des déclarations d'internautes, avec toutes les entrées et hypothèses affichées.

facts.label: Ce qui est demandé
facts.value: ville de départ, ville d'arrivée, taille du logement, date

paragraphs: Le calcul se fait ici sur Livdar. Les entrées sont affichées, les hypothèses sont écrites, et le résultat est une fourchette plutôt qu'un nombre unique partout où les données sous-jacentes ne permettent qu'une fourchette.

La question est de savoir ce que coûte le déménagement d'un foyer, et c'est le seul outil ici sans institut statistique derrière lui, parce qu'aucun institut ne publie de prix de déménagement. Le modèle est celui de Livdar : volume, distance, heures d'équipe, emballage, assurance et la manutention qu'ajoute un passage de frontière. Le volume au delà d'un véhicule devient un second voyage, et c'est la marche qu'une estimation linéaire rate, ce qui explique les devis en ligne trop bas. La réponse est toujours une fourchette avec ses hypothèses, jamais un nombre unique, et jamais un devis.
Exemple chiffré : un trois pièces déplacé de cinq cents kilomètres se situe entre 1 095 et 1 715 euros, et l'outil dit quelles hypothèses produisent chaque borne.

La méthode n'est ni secrète ni un modèle qu'il faudrait croire sur parole. L'outil lit les valeurs publiées dans Livdar, applique le calcul décrit sur la page et affiche l'année de chaque valeur utilisée, de sorte que qui conteste le résultat voit exactement quel chiffre il conteste.

faq.q: D'où viennent les chiffres ?
faq.a: Le calcul porte sur Livdar. Chaque valeur utilisée cite l'institution qui l'a publiée et l'année qu'elle décrit.

faq.q: Le résultat est-il un devis ?
faq.a: Non. C'est une estimation issue de statistiques publiées, et elle dit lesquelles et pour quelle année. Ce qui engage vient de celui qui va vous facturer.

facts.label: Ce qui est demandé
facts.value: destination, nombre de nuits, style de voyage

paragraphs: Le calcul se fait ici sur Eurostat + World Bank. Les entrées sont affichées, les hypothèses sont écrites, et le résultat est une fourchette plutôt qu'un nombre unique partout où les données sous-jacentes ne permettent qu'une fourchette.

La question est de savoir ce que coûte un voyage par jour, ce qui n'est pas la question du coût de la vie dans un pays et se traite avec la même source lue autrement. Le panier d'un résident pèse sur le loyer et l'énergie, celui d'un visiteur sur les restaurants, les hôtels et les transports, et ces trois postes sont publiés séparément, donc l'estimation s'appuie sur eux plutôt que sur le chiffre d'ensemble. Elle ne peut pas chiffrer un hôtel précis ni un vol précis, et un outil qui le prétendrait lirait un niveau des prix comme s'il était un moteur de réservation.
Exemple chiffré : Suisse face à Turquie. Le même panier normalisé y coûte environ 294 pour cent de plus dans le premier, sur les valeurs de 2024.
La couverture porte sur 199 pays, exactement ceux que mesure la source et pas un de plus.

Les chiffres derrière cet outil décrivent 2024 et changent quand Eurostat + World Bank publie, pas quand cette page est modifiée. C'est pourquoi l'année figure à côté de chaque valeur et non en bas de page : un outil dont les données ont un an et qui le dit est plus utile qu'un outil qui a l'air à jour sans l'être.

pages.title: Cheapest countries in Europe: the measured list
pages.description: Cheapest countries in Europe, ranked on one measure across 37 countries for 2024. Every figure is quoted as index, EU average = 100 and cites the institution that published it.
paragraphs: Türkiye comes top of this list at 46.8, out of 37 countries measured on the same scale for 2024. The measure is a price level quoted as index, EU average = 100.

Europe is the one place where this comparison is on firm ground. Almost every country here is measured by the same institution on the same definition in the same year, which is rarely true of a world list, so the gaps between neighbours mean what they appear to mean. It also makes the spread visible: the distance between the cheapest and the dearest country inside a single continent and largely a single market is wider than most people expect.

The list sorts on one measure, the Eurostat household price level index, quoted as index, EU average = 100, and it covers 37 of the roughly 47 countries it claims. Nothing is blended: a list that mixed two price measures on two scales would be ordering two different things and would put currency regimes at the top rather than cheap countries.
A price level is not a cost of living for a person. It compares a standard basket across countries and takes no account of what you earn, where you live inside the country, or what you actually buy.

faq.q: Why are some countries missing?
faq.a: Because they are not measured on this scale. 37 countries carry a value for this measure, and adding a country from the other scale would break the ordering rather than extend it.

faq.q: What does the number mean?
faq.a: It is a price level quoted as index, EU average = 100. A country at twice another country is roughly twice as expensive for the same standard basket.

pages.title: Average salary in Germany: gross, net and the minimum wage
pages.description: What Germany pays, from the official European earnings series: net pay averages 3,045 euro a month for 2025, shown next to gross pay and the statutory minimum.
paragraphs: Germany pays 4,834 euro a month on average before tax and 3,045 euro after, measured for 2025. Both figures describe a single person without children on the average wage, which is the case the source publishes.
Germany takes about 37 percent of a gross wage in income tax and social contributions, which is the gap between the two figures above rather than a rate anybody is charged.
The statutory minimum wage is 2,343 euro a month for 2026.
Germany ranks 8 of 27 countries in the series on net pay, where the middle country is at 2,106 euro a month.
That puts Germany about 44.6 percent above the median of these 27 countries, which is 2,106 a month.
On the same series Germany sits between Finland at 3,141 and Belgium at 3,035, which is what a rank on its own does not tell you.

Pay only means something next to prices. The same source puts the price level in Germany at 109.1 on the index, EU average = 100 for 2024, so a wage that looks high or low against its neighbours may not be once the cost of the basket is put beside it.
An average is not a typical salary. It is pulled upward by high earners, it says nothing about any particular job, and it is worth reading next to the cost of living rather than on its own.

faq.q: Is this before or after tax?
faq.a: Both are shown. Gross is before income tax and social contributions, net is after, and the difference between them is the wedge figure on this page.

faq.q: Does this mean I would earn 3,045 euro a month in Germany?
faq.a: No. This is the average for a single person on the average wage in 2025. What any individual earns depends on the occupation, the sector, the region and the employer, none of which this series splits out.

pages.title: Custo de vida na Espanha: o que o nível de preços diz de facto
pages.description: Espanha: quanto custa viver lá, medido e não estimado: o nível de preços é de 90,7 para 2024, com a divisão por categorias e a fonte de cada número.

facts.label: Tudo o que uma família compra

paragraphs: A Espanha tem um nível de preços de 90,7 quando a média da União Europeia vale 100, medido para 2024. Um cabaz de consumo custa lá cerca de 9 por cento a menos do que o mesmo cabaz no conjunto da União.
Para este país são publicadas doze categorias de despesa, por isso a divisão abaixo é medida e não deduzida do número global.
Dentro do cabaz a distância é maior do que o número global sugere. A categoria mais cara é Habitação, água e energia, com 96,5, e a mais barata Restaurantes e hotéis, com 83,9.
A Espanha: os preços subiram 2,7 por cento no ano até 2024, pelo que os números acima já terão andado um pouco desde que foram recolhidos.
A Espanha ocupa a posição 19 entre os 39 países que esta fonte mede na mesma escala, o que o coloca na metade mais barata desse grupo.
Na mesma escala fica entre Japão com 89 e Eslovênia com 91, que é a companhia real por trás de um lugar 19 em 39.
Diretamente comparável com outros 38 países medidos na mesma escala.

Um nível de preços não é um orçamento. Compara um cabaz padronizado entre países e não sabe nada do que ganha, da distância entre a capital e uma vila, nem do que paga de renda quem acaba de chegar face a quem já lá mora há anos. Leia-o como ponto de partida para comparar e não como um número com que fazer planos.

faq.a: É o valor recolhido para 2024. As estatísticas de nível de preços são anuais e chegam sempre com atraso, por isso esta é a última publicada e não um número de hoje.

pages.h1: Los países más baratos de Europa
pages.title: Los países más baratos de Europa: la lista medida
pages.description: Los países más baratos de Europa, ordenados por un solo indicador entre 37 países para 2024. Cada valor se da en índice, media de la UE = 100 y cita a la institución que lo publicó.

facts.label: Indicador
facts.value: Todo lo que compra un hogar

paragraphs: En cabeza de esta lista está Turquía con 46,8, de 37 países medidos en la misma escala para 2024. El indicador es un nivel de precios expresado en índice, media de la UE = 100.

Europa es el único sitio donde esta comparación pisa terreno firme. Casi todos los países de aquí los mide la misma institución con la misma definición y el mismo año, cosa que rara vez pasa en una lista mundial, así que las distancias entre vecinos significan lo que parecen significar. Eso también deja ver la amplitud: la distancia entre el país más barato y el más caro dentro de un continente y en buena medida de un solo mercado es mayor de lo que casi nadie espera.

La lista se ordena por un solo indicador, el índice de nivel de precios de consumo de Eurostat, expresado en índice, media de la UE = 100, y cubre 37 de los aproximadamente 47 países que reclama su título. No se mezcla nada: una lista que juntara dos medidas de precios en dos escalas estaría ordenando dos cosas distintas y subiría regímenes cambiarios en lugar de países baratos.
Un nivel de precios no es el coste de vida de una persona. Compara una cesta normalizada entre países y no sabe nada de lo que ganas, de dónde vives dentro del país ni de lo que compras de verdad.

paragraphs: En cabeza de esta lista está Turquía con 46,8, de 37 países medidos en la misma escala para 2024. El indicador es un nivel de precios expresado en índice, media de la UE = 100.

Europa es el único sitio donde esta comparación pisa terreno firme. Casi todos los países de aquí los mide la misma institución con la misma definición y el mismo año, cosa que rara vez pasa en una lista mundial, así que las distancias entre vecinos significan lo que parecen significar. Eso también deja ver la amplitud: la distancia entre el país más barato y el más caro dentro de un continente y en buena medida de un solo mercado es mayor de lo que casi nadie espera.

La lista se ordena por un solo indicador, el índice de nivel de precios de consumo de Eurostat, expresado en índice, media de la UE = 100, y cubre 37 de los aproximadamente 47 países que reclama su título. No se mezcla nada: una lista que juntara dos medidas de precios en dos escalas estaría ordenando dos cosas distintas y subiría regímenes cambiarios en lugar de países baratos.
Un nivel de precios no es el coste de vida de una persona. Compara una cesta normalizada entre países y no sabe nada de lo que ganas, de dónde vives dentro del país ni de lo que compras de verdad.

paragraphs: Die Schweiz hat ein Preisniveau von 184,3, wobei der Durchschnitt der Europäischen Union bei 100 liegt, gemessen für 2024. Ein Warenkorb kostet dort rund 84 Prozent mehr als im Unionsdurchschnitt.
Für dieses Land werden zwölf Warengruppen veröffentlicht, die Aufschlüsselung unten ist also gemessen und nicht aus der Gesamtzahl abgeleitet.
Innerhalb des Warenkorbs ist die Spanne größer, als die Gesamtzahl vermuten lässt. Am teuersten ist die Gruppe Bildung mit 269,9, am günstigsten Verkehr mit 126,9.
Die Schweiz: Die Preise stiegen im Jahr bis 2024 um 0,1 Prozent, die Werte oben haben sich seit der Erhebung also leicht verschoben.
Die Schweiz liegt auf Platz 39 der 39 Länder, die diese Quelle auf derselben Skala misst, und damit in der teureren Hälfte dieser Gruppe.
Nichts auf dieser Skala ist teurer. Das nächste Land darunter ist Island mit 172,7, von 39 gleich gemessenen Ländern.
Direkt vergleichbar mit 38 weiteren Ländern auf derselben Skala.

Ein Preisniveau ist kein Budget. Es vergleicht einen genormten Warenkorb zwischen Ländern und weiß nichts davon, was Sie verdienen, wie weit Hauptstadt und Kleinstadt auseinanderliegen oder was ein Zuziehender für Miete zahlt im Unterschied zu einem langjährigen Mieter. pages.title: Average salary in Greece: gross, net and the minimum wage
pages.description: What Greece pays, from the official European earnings series: net pay averages 1,792 euro a month for 2025, shown next to gross pay and the statutory minimum.
paragraphs: Greece pays 2,471 euro a month on average before tax and 1,792 euro after, measured for 2025. Both figures describe a single person without children on the average wage, which is the case the source publishes.
Greece takes about 27.5 percent of a gross wage in income tax and social contributions, which is the gap between the two figures above rather than a rate anybody is charged.
The statutory minimum wage is 1,073 euro a month for 2026.
Greece ranks 17 of 27 countries in the series on net pay, where the middle country is at 2,106 euro a month.
That puts Greece about 14.9 percent below the median of these 27 countries, which is 2,106 a month.
On the same series Greece sits between Estonia at 1,878 and Portugal at 1,787, which is what a rank on its own does not tell you.

Pay only means something next to prices. The same source puts the price level in Greece at 83 on the index, EU average = 100 for 2024, so a wage that looks high or low against its neighbours may not be once the cost of the basket is put beside it.
An average is not a typical salary. It is pulled upward by high earners, it says nothing about any particular job, and it is worth reading next to the cost of living rather than on its own.

faq.q: Is this before or after tax?
faq.a: Both are shown. Gross is before income tax and social contributions, net is after, and the difference between them is the wedge figure on this page.

faq.q: Does this mean I would earn 1,792 euro a month in Greece?
faq.a: No. This is the average for a single person on the average wage in 2025. What any individual earns depends on the occupation, the sector, the region and the employer, none of which this series splits out.

Per questo paese vengono pubblicate dodici categorie di spesa, quindi il dettaglio qui sotto è misurato e non dedotto dalla cifra complessiva.
Dentro il paniere la distanza è più ampia di quanto suggerisca la cifra complessiva. La categoria più cara è Salute, a 116,6, la più economica Telefono e internet, a 85,7.

L'Italia occupa la posizione 24 fra i 39 paesi che questa fonte misura sulla stessa scala, e sta quindi nella metà più cara di quel gruppo.

Direttamente confrontabile con altri 38 paesi misurati sulla stessa scala.

pages.title: Custo de vida na Irlanda: o que o nível de preços diz de facto
pages.description: Irlanda: quanto custa viver lá, medido e não estimado: o nível de preços é de 141,2 para 2024, com a divisão por categorias e a fonte de cada número.

facts.label: Tudo o que uma família compra

paragraphs: A Irlanda tem um nível de preços de 141,2 quando a média da União Europeia vale 100, medido para 2024. Um cabaz de consumo custa lá cerca de 41 por cento a mais do que o mesmo cabaz no conjunto da União.
Para este país são publicadas doze categorias de despesa, por isso a divisão abaixo é medida e não deduzida do número global.
Dentro do cabaz a distância é maior do que o número global sugere. A categoria mais cara é Álcool e tabaco, com 204,5, e a mais barata Roupa e calçado, com 100,2.
A Irlanda: os preços subiram 2,1 por cento no ano até 2024, pelo que os números acima já terão andado um pouco desde que foram recolhidos.
A Irlanda ocupa a posição 34 entre os 39 países que esta fonte mede na mesma escala, o que o coloca na metade mais cara desse grupo.
Na mesma escala fica entre Noruega com 134,1 e Dinamarca com 142,8, que é a companhia real por trás de um lugar 34 em 39.
Diretamente comparável com outros 38 países medidos na mesma escala.

Um nível de preços não é um orçamento. Compara um cabaz padronizado entre países e não sabe nada do que ganha, da distância entre a capital e uma vila, nem do que paga de renda quem acaba de chegar face a quem já lá mora há anos. Leia-o como ponto de partida para comparar e não como um número com que fazer planos.

pages.h1: Os países mais baratos da Europa
pages.title: Os países mais baratos da Europa: a lista medida
pages.description: Os países mais baratos da Europa, ordenados por um único indicador entre 37 países para 2024. Cada valor está em índice, média da UE = 100 e cita a instituição que o publicou.

facts.label: Indicador
facts.value: Tudo o que uma família compra

paragraphs: No topo desta lista está Turquia com 46,8, de 37 países medidos na mesma escala para 2024. O indicador é um nível de preços expresso em índice, média da UE = 100.

A Europa é o único sítio onde esta comparação assenta em terreno firme. Quase todos os países aqui são medidos pela mesma instituição, com a mesma definição e no mesmo ano, o que raramente acontece numa lista mundial, por isso as distâncias entre vizinhos querem dizer o que parecem querer dizer. Isso deixa também ver a amplitude: a distância entre o país mais barato e o mais caro dentro de um continente e em boa parte de um só mercado é maior do que quase toda a gente espera.

A lista ordena por um único indicador, o índice Eurostat do nível de preços no consumo, expresso em índice, média da UE = 100, e cobre 37 dos cerca de 47 países que o título reivindica. Nada é misturado: uma lista que juntasse duas medidas de preços em duas escalas estaria a ordenar duas coisas diferentes e levaria regimes cambiais para o topo em vez de países baratos.
Um nível de preços não é o custo de vida de uma pessoa. Compara um cabaz padronizado entre países e não sabe nada do que ganha, de onde vive dentro do país nem do que compra de facto.

pages.title: Salaris calculator: op gemeten data
pages.description: Salaris calculator van Livdar, berekend op Eurostat en niet op door gebruikers ingestuurde cijfers, met alle invoer en aannames in het zicht.
paragraphs: De berekening steunt hier op Eurostat. De invoer staat in het zicht, de aannames staan opgeschreven, en de uitkomst is een bandbreedte in plaats van één getal overal waar de onderliggende data alleen een bandbreedte toelaat.

De vraag is wat werk in het ene land oplevert tegenover het andere, gemeten volgens dezelfde definitie aan beide kanten. De gepubliceerde reeks dekt een alleenstaande met een gemiddeld loon, voor en na inhoudingen, en dat is de enige vergelijking die over de grens standhoudt: een brutoloon wordt in het buurland anders belast, en twee brutobedragen uit twee belastingstelsels zijn niet twee keer hetzelfde getal. Wat het niet kan, is een bepaalde baan waarderen. Beroep, sector, ervaring en werkgever bewegen het loon meer dan het land, en daar zit niets van in deze reeks.
Rekenvoorbeeld: Oostenrijk in 2025. Van 5.219 euro bruto per maand blijft na belasting en premies 3.529 euro over, een verschil van 32,4 procent.
De dekking is 35 landen, precies de verzameling die de bron meet en geen land meer.

De cijfers achter dit hulpmiddel beschrijven 2025 en veranderen wanneer Eurostat publiceert, niet wanneer deze pagina bewerkt wordt. Daarom staat het jaar naast elke waarde en niet in de kleine lettertjes: een hulpmiddel waarvan de data een jaar oud is en dat dat zegt, is nuttiger dan een dat actueel lijkt en het niet is.

faq.q: Waar komen de cijfers vandaan?
faq.a: De berekening steunt op Eurostat. Elke gebruikte waarde noemt de instelling die haar publiceerde en het jaar dat zij beschrijft.

faq.q: Is de uitkomst een offerte?
faq.a: Nee. Het is een schatting uit gepubliceerde statistiek, en er staat bij welke en over welk jaar. Bindend wordt het pas bij wie u straks factureert.

pages.title: Average salary in Denmark: gross, net and the minimum wage
pages.description: What Denmark pays, from the official European earnings series: net pay averages 3,786 euro a month for 2025, shown next to gross pay and the statutory minimum.
paragraphs: Denmark pays 5,968 euro a month on average before tax and 3,786 euro after, measured for 2025. Both figures describe a single person without children on the average wage, which is the case the source publishes.
Denmark takes about 36.6 percent of a gross wage in income tax and social contributions, which is the gap between the two figures above rather than a rate anybody is charged.
Denmark has no statutory minimum wage set in law. Pay floors there are set by collective agreement per sector, so there is no single national number to quote.
Denmark ranks 3 of 27 countries in the series on net pay, where the middle country is at 2,106 euro a month.
That puts Denmark about 79.8 percent above the median of these 27 countries, which is 2,106 a month.
On the same series Denmark sits between Ireland at 3,919 and Austria at 3,529, which is what a rank on its own does not tell you.

Pay only means something next to prices. The same source puts the price level in Denmark at 142.8 on the index, EU average = 100 for 2024, so a wage that looks high or low against its neighbours may not be once the cost of the basket is put beside it.
An average is not a typical salary. It is pulled upward by high earners, it says nothing about any particular job, and it is worth reading next to the cost of living rather than on its own.

faq.q: Is this before or after tax?
faq.a: Both are shown. Gross is before income tax and social contributions, net is after, and the difference between them is the wedge figure on this page.

faq.q: Does this mean I would earn 3,786 euro a month in Denmark?
faq.a: No. This is the average for a single person on the average wage in 2025. What any individual earns depends on the occupation, the sector, the region and the employer, none of which this series splits out.

pages.title: Lebenshaltungskosten Dänemark: was das Preisniveau wirklich aussagt
pages.description: Was Dänemark kostet, gemessen statt geschätzt: Das Preisniveau liegt bei 142,8 für das Jahr 2024, mit allen Warengruppen und der Quelle hinter jeder Zahl.
paragraphs: Dänemark hat ein Preisniveau von 142,8, wobei der Durchschnitt der Europäischen Union bei 100 liegt, gemessen für 2024. Ein Warenkorb kostet dort rund 43 Prozent mehr als im Unionsdurchschnitt.
Für dieses Land werden zwölf Warengruppen veröffentlicht, die Aufschlüsselung unten ist also gemessen und nicht aus der Gesamtzahl abgeleitet.
Innerhalb des Warenkorbs ist die Spanne größer, als die Gesamtzahl vermuten lässt. Am teuersten ist die Gruppe Wohnen, Wasser und Energie mit 185,5, am günstigsten Telefon und Internet mit 108,7.
Dänemark: Die Preise stiegen im Jahr bis 2024 um 1,8 Prozent, die Werte oben haben sich seit der Erhebung also leicht verschoben.
Dänemark liegt auf Platz 35 der 39 Länder, die diese Quelle auf derselben Skala misst, und damit in der teureren Hälfte dieser Gruppe.
Auf derselben Skala liegt es zwischen Irland mit 141,2 und Vereinigte Staaten mit 149,2. Das ist die Gesellschaft, in die Platz 35 von 39 es tatsächlich stellt.
Direkt vergleichbar mit 38 weiteren Ländern auf derselben Skala.

Ein Preisniveau ist kein Budget. Es vergleicht einen genormten Warenkorb zwischen Ländern und weiß nichts davon, was Sie verdienen, wie weit Hauptstadt und Kleinstadt auseinanderliegen oder was ein Zuziehender für Miete zahlt im Unterschied zu einem langjährigen Mieter. Lesen Sie es als Ausgangspunkt für einen Vergleich und nicht als Zahl, mit der sich planen lässt.

pages.title: Costo della vita in Giappone: che cosa dicono davvero i prezzi
pages.description: Giappone: quanto costa viverci, misurato e non stimato: il livello dei prezzi è 89 per il 2024, con il dettaglio per categoria e la fonte dietro ogni cifra.

facts.label: Tutto quello che compra una famiglia

paragraphs: Il Giappone ha un livello dei prezzi di 89 quando la media dell'Unione europea vale 100, misurato per il 2024. Un paniere di consumo vi costa circa il 11 per cento in meno dello stesso paniere nell'Unione.

Di questo paese viene pubblicato solo il livello dei prezzi complessivo. Il dettaglio in dodici categorie esiste per gli stati membri dell'Unione europea e non per questo, e qui nulla riempie quel vuoto con una stima.
In questa fonte non c'è una serie annuale di inflazione per il Giappone, quindi da qui non si può dire di quanto il valore si sia spostato da quando è stato rilevato.
Il Giappone occupa la posizione 18 fra i 39 paesi che questa fonte misura sulla stessa scala, e sta quindi nella metà più economica di quel gruppo.
Sulla stessa scala si colloca tra Portogallo con 85 e Spagna con 90,7, che è la compagnia reale dietro un posto 18 su 39.
Direttamente confrontabile con altri 38 paesi misurati sulla stessa scala.

Un livello dei prezzi non è un bilancio. Confronta un paniere standard fra paesi e non sa nulla di quanto guadagni, della distanza fra la capitale e un paese di provincia, né di quanto paga di affitto chi arriva adesso rispetto a chi ci abita da anni. Va letto come punto di partenza per un confronto e non come una cifra su cui fare i conti.

pages.title: タイの生活費：物価水準が実際に示すもの
pages.description: タイの生活費を、推計ではなく測定値で。2025年の物価水準は 0.31。品目別の内訳と、数値ごとの出典つき。
paragraphs: タイの物価水準は、米国を 1 としたとき 0.31（2025年の測定）。財とサービスの価格は米国よりおよそ 69 パーセント安い。
この国は欧州の物価水準指数ではなく、世界銀行の比率で捕捉されている。より粗い、別の尺度の指標であり、欧州指数で示された数値と並べて比べることはできない。
この出典にはタイの年次インフレ系列がない。そのため測定時点からどれだけずれたかは、ここからは言えない。
この出典が同じ尺度で測っている 160 か国のうち、タイは安いほうから 27 番目にあたり、そのグループの安いほうの半分に入る。
同じ尺度ではマダガスカルの0.307とウクライナの0.31の間に位置します。160か国中27位という順位が実際に意味するのはこの並びです。
同じ尺度で測定された他の 159 か国と直接比較できる。
物価水準は家計の予算ではない。国どうしで標準化した買い物かごを比べるだけで、収入も、首都と地方の差も、長く住んでいる人の家賃と新しく来た人が払う家賃の違いも織り込んでいない。比較の出発点として読むべきで、これをもとに計画を立てる数字ではない。

faq.q: タイの物価は高いですか。
faq.a: この数値が用いる基準に対して、2025年の物価水準は 0.31 です。このページが誠実に言えるのはここまでで、物価水準が表すのは買い物かごであってあなたの暮らしではありません。

faq.q: この数値は何年のものですか。
faq.a: 2025年について記録された値です。物価水準の統計は年次で必ず遅れて出るため、これは最新の公表値であり今日の数値ではありません。

faq.q: 他の国と比べられますか。
faq.a: 同じ尺度で測定された国とだけです。この値の単位は 比率、米国 = 1 で、別の尺度にある国とは、誰も測定していない換算を挟まないかぎり比較になりません。

paragraphs: この一覧の先頭は トルコ で 46.8。2024年に同じ尺度で測定された 37 か国の中での順位である。指標は単位 指数、EU平均 = 100 の物価水準。
この比較が確かな足場に立てる唯一の場所がヨーロッパである。ここに並ぶ国のほとんどは、同じ機関が同じ定義で同じ年に測っている。世界規模の一覧ではまず成り立たない条件で、だから隣国どうしの差は見た目どおりの意味を持つ。開きも見えてくる。一つの大陸、しかも大部分は一つの市場のなかで、最も安い国と最も高い国の距離は、たいていの人が思うより広い。
並べ替えは単一の指標 ユーロスタットの家計消費物価水準指数（単位 指数、EU平均 = 100）だけで行い、題名が対象とする約 47 か国のうち 37 か国を収めている。混ぜることはしない。二つの尺度の物価指標を混ぜた一覧は、異なる二つのものを並べることになり、物価の安い国ではなく通貨制度を上位に押し上げてしまう。
物価水準は個人の生活費ではない。国どうしで標準化した買い物かごを比べるもので、収入も、国内のどこに住むかも、実際に何を買うかも織り込んでいない。

pages.title: Preventivo trasloco: su dati misurati
pages.description: Preventivo trasloco di Livdar, calcolato su Livdar e non su segnalazioni degli utenti, con tutti gli ingressi e le ipotesi in chiaro.

facts.label: Che cosa chiede
facts.value: città di partenza, città di arrivo, dimensione dell'abitazione, data

paragraphs: Il calcolo qui si appoggia a Livdar. Gli ingressi sono in chiaro, le ipotesi sono scritte e il risultato è un intervallo invece di un numero secco ovunque i dati di partenza reggano solo un intervallo.

La domanda è quanto costa spostare una casa da un posto a un altro, ed è l'unico strumento qui senza un istituto di statistica dietro, perché nessun istituto pubblica i prezzi dei traslochi. Il modello è di Livdar: volume, distanza, ore di squadra, imballaggio, assicurazione e la movimentazione che aggiunge un confine. Il volume che non sta in un veicolo diventa un secondo viaggio, ed è il gradino che una stima lineare salta e il motivo per cui i preventivi online costano troppo poco. La risposta è sempre un intervallo con le sue ipotesi, mai un numero secco, e mai un preventivo.
Esempio con i numeri: un trilocale spostato di cinquecento chilometri viene fra 1095 e 1715 euro, e lo strumento dice quali ipotesi producono ciascun estremo.

Il metodo non è segreto e non è un modello da prendere per buono. Lo strumento legge i valori pubblicati in Livdar, applica il conto descritto nella pagina e mostra l'anno di ogni valore usato, così chi non è d'accordo con il risultato vede esattamente con quale numero non è d'accordo.

faq.q: Da dove vengono i numeri?
faq.a: Il calcolo si appoggia a Livdar. Ogni valore usato porta con sé l'istituzione che lo ha pubblicato e l'anno che descrive.

faq.q: Il risultato è un preventivo?
faq.a: No. È una stima da statistiche pubblicate, e dice quali e di che anno. Quello che impegna arriva da chi poi ti fattura.

pages.title: Average salary in Ireland: gross, net and the minimum wage
pages.description: What Ireland pays, from the official European earnings series: net pay averages 3,919 euro a month for 2025, shown next to gross pay and the statutory minimum.
paragraphs: Ireland pays 5,143 euro a month on average before tax and 3,919 euro after, measured for 2025. Both figures describe a single person without children on the average wage, which is the case the source publishes.
Ireland takes about 23.8 percent of a gross wage in income tax and social contributions, which is the gap between the two figures above rather than a rate anybody is charged.
The statutory minimum wage is 2,391 euro a month for 2026.
Ireland ranks 2 of 27 countries in the series on net pay, where the middle country is at 2,106 euro a month.
That puts Ireland about 86.1 percent above the median of these 27 countries, which is 2,106 a month.
On the same series Ireland sits between Luxembourg at 4,656 and Denmark at 3,786, which is what a rank on its own does not tell you.

Pay only means something next to prices. The same source puts the price level in Ireland at 141.2 on the index, EU average = 100 for 2024, so a wage that looks high or low against its neighbours may not be once the cost of the basket is put beside it.
An average is not a typical salary. It is pulled upward by high earners, it says nothing about any particular job, and it is worth reading next to the cost of living rather than on its own.

faq.q: Is this before or after tax?
faq.a: Both are shown. Gross is before income tax and social contributions, net is after, and the difference between them is the wedge figure on this page.

pages.title: Lebenshaltungskosten Bulgarien: was das Preisniveau wirklich aussagt
pages.description: Was Bulgarien kostet, gemessen statt geschätzt: Das Preisniveau liegt bei 56,9 für das Jahr 2024, mit allen Warengruppen und der Quelle hinter jeder Zahl.
paragraphs: Bulgarien hat ein Preisniveau von 56,9, wobei der Durchschnitt der Europäischen Union bei 100 liegt, gemessen für 2024. Ein Warenkorb kostet dort rund 43 Prozent weniger als im Unionsdurchschnitt.
Für dieses Land werden zwölf Warengruppen veröffentlicht, die Aufschlüsselung unten ist also gemessen und nicht aus der Gesamtzahl abgeleitet.

Innerhalb des Warenkorbs ist die Spanne größer, als die Gesamtzahl vermuten lässt. Am teuersten ist die Gruppe Lebensmittel und alkoholfreie Getränke mit 88,8, am günstigsten Wohnen, Wasser und Energie mit 38,1.
Bulgarien: Die Preise stiegen im Jahr bis 2024 um 3,5 Prozent, die Werte oben haben sich seit der Erhebung also leicht verschoben.
Bulgarien liegt auf Platz 3 der 39 Länder, die diese Quelle auf derselben Skala misst, und damit in der günstigeren Hälfte dieser Gruppe.
Auf derselben Skala liegt es zwischen Nordmazedonien mit 49,6 und Rumänien mit 57,4. Das ist die Gesellschaft, in die Platz 3 von 39 es tatsächlich stellt.
Direkt vergleichbar mit 38 weiteren Ländern auf derselben Skala.

Ein Preisniveau ist kein Budget. Es vergleicht einen genormten Warenkorb zwischen Ländern und weiß nichts davon, was Sie verdienen, wie weit Hauptstadt und Kleinstadt auseinanderliegen oder was ein Zuziehender für Miete zahlt im Unterschied zu einem langjährigen Mieter. Lesen Sie es als Ausgangspunkt für einen Vergleich und nicht als Zahl, mit der sich planen lässt.

faq.q: Bulgarien: ist das Leben dort teuer?
faq.a: Gemessen an der Bezugsgröße dieser Zahl liegt das Preisniveau bei 56,9 für 2024. Mehr lässt sich hier ehrlich nicht sagen, denn ein Preisniveau beschreibt einen Warenkorb und nicht Ihr Leben.

faq.q: Aus welchem Jahr stammt der Wert?
faq.a: Es ist der für 2024 erhobene Wert. Preisniveaustatistiken erscheinen jährlich und hinken immer hinterher, das hier ist also der zuletzt veröffentlichte Wert und keine Zahl für heute.

faq.q: Kann ich das mit einem anderen Land vergleichen?
faq.a: Nur mit Ländern auf derselben Skala. Dieser Wert ist als Index, EU-Durchschnitt = 100 angegeben, ein Land auf der anderen Skala ist damit ohne eine Umrechnung, die niemand gemessen hat, nicht vergleichbar.

pages.title: Custo de vida na Alemanha: o que o nível de preços diz de facto
pages.description: Alemanha: quanto custa viver lá, medido e não estimado: o nível de preços é de 109,1 para 2024, com a divisão por categorias e a fonte de cada número.

facts.label: Tudo o que uma família compra

paragraphs: A Alemanha tem um nível de preços de 109,1 quando a média da União Europeia vale 100, medido para 2024. Um cabaz de consumo custa lá cerca de 9 por cento a mais do que o mesmo cabaz no conjunto da União.
Para este país são publicadas doze categorias de despesa, por isso a divisão abaixo é medida e não deduzida do número global.
Dentro do cabaz a distância é maior do que o número global sugere. A categoria mais cara é Telefone e internet, com 136, e a mais barata Álcool e tabaco, com 99,6.
A Alemanha: os preços subiram 2,3 por cento no ano até 2024, pelo que os números acima já terão andado um pouco desde que foram recolhidos.
A Alemanha ocupa a posição 26 entre os 39 países que esta fonte mede na mesma escala, o que o coloca na metade mais cara desse grupo.
Na mesma escala fica entre França com 107,9 e Bélgica com 118,7, que é a companhia real por trás de um lugar 26 em 39.
Diretamente comparável com outros 38 países medidos na mesma escala.

Um nível de preços não é um orçamento. Compara um cabaz padronizado entre países e não sabe nada do que ganha, da distância entre a capital e uma vila, nem do que paga de renda quem acaba de chegar face a quem já lá mora há anos. Leia-o como ponto de partida para comparar e não como um número com que fazer planos.

pages.description: Was Japan kostet, gemessen statt geschätzt: Das Preisniveau liegt bei 89 für das Jahr 2024, mit allen Warengruppen und der Quelle hinter jeder Zahl.
paragraphs: Japan hat ein Preisniveau von 89, wobei der Durchschnitt der Europäischen Union bei 100 liegt, gemessen für 2024. Ein Warenkorb kostet dort rund 11 Prozent weniger als im Unionsdurchschnitt.

Für dieses Land wird nur das Gesamtpreisniveau veröffentlicht. Die Aufschlüsselung in zwölf Gruppen gibt es für die Mitgliedstaaten der Europäischen Union und für dieses Land nicht, und nichts hier füllt diese Lücke mit einer Schätzung.
Für Japan gibt es in dieser Quelle keine jährliche Inflationsreihe. Wie weit sich der Wert seit der Erhebung verschoben hat, lässt sich hier also nicht sagen.
Japan liegt auf Platz 18 der 39 Länder, die diese Quelle auf derselben Skala misst, und damit in der günstigeren Hälfte dieser Gruppe.
Auf derselben Skala liegt es zwischen Portugal mit 85 und Spanien mit 90,7. Das ist die Gesellschaft, in die Platz 18 von 39 es tatsächlich stellt.
Direkt vergleichbar mit 38 weiteren Ländern auf derselben Skala.

Ein Preisniveau ist kein Budget. Es vergleicht einen genormten Warenkorb zwischen Ländern und weiß nichts davon, was Sie verdienen, wie weit Hauptstadt und Kleinstadt auseinanderliegen oder was ein Zuziehender für Miete zahlt im Unterschied zu einem langjährigen Mieter. faq.a: Gemessen an der Bezugsgröße dieser Zahl liegt das Preisniveau bei 89 für 2024. Mehr lässt sich hier ehrlich nicht sagen, denn ein Preisniveau beschreibt einen Warenkorb und nicht Ihr Leben.

faq.a: Es ist der für 2024 erhobene Wert. Preisniveaustatistiken erscheinen jährlich und hinken immer hinterher, das hier ist also der zuletzt veröffentlichte Wert und keine Zahl für heute.

pages.title: Average salary in Romania: gross, net and the minimum wage
pages.description: What Romania pays, from the official European earnings series: net pay averages 1,156 euro a month for 2025, shown next to gross pay and the statutory minimum.
paragraphs: Romania pays 1,977 euro a month on average before tax and 1,156 euro after, measured for 2025. Both figures describe a single person without children on the average wage, which is the case the source publishes.
Romania takes about 41.5 percent of a gross wage in income tax and social contributions, which is the gap between the two figures above rather than a rate anybody is charged.
The statutory minimum wage is 825 euro a month for 2026.
Romania ranks 27 of 27 countries in the series on net pay, where the middle country is at 2,106 euro a month.
That puts Romania about 45.1 percent below the median of these 27 countries, which is 2,106 a month.
Romania is at the bottom of this series, with Bulgaria at 1,204 directly above it.

Pay only means something next to prices. The same source puts the price level in Romania at 57.4 on the index, EU average = 100 for 2024, so a wage that looks high or low against its neighbours may not be once the cost of the basket is put beside it.
An average is not a typical salary. It is pulled upward by high earners, it says nothing about any particular job, and it is worth reading next to the cost of living rather than on its own.

faq.q: Is this before or after tax?
faq.a: Both are shown. Gross is before income tax and social contributions, net is after, and the difference between them is the wedge figure on this page.

faq.q: Does this mean I would earn 1,156 euro a month in Romania?
faq.a: No. This is the average for a single person on the average wage in 2025. What any individual earns depends on the occupation, the sector, the region and the employer, none of which this series splits out.

pages.h1: Coût de la vie au Japon
pages.title: Coût de la vie au Japon : ce que disent vraiment les prix
pages.description: Japon : ce que coûte la vie, mesuré et non estimé : le niveau des prix est de 89 pour 2024, avec le détail par poste et la source de chaque chiffre.
paragraphs: Le Japon a un niveau des prix de 89 quand la moyenne de l'Union européenne vaut 100, mesuré pour 2024. Un panier de consommation y coûte environ 11 pour cent de moins que le même panier dans l'Union.

Seul le niveau des prix d'ensemble est publié pour ce pays. Le détail en douze postes existe pour les membres de l'Union européenne et pas pour celui-ci, et rien ici ne comble ce vide par une estimation.
Aucune série annuelle d'inflation ne couvre ce pays dans cette source. Impossible donc de dire ici de combien la valeur a bougé depuis son relevé.
Le Japon occupe le rang 18 des 39 pays que cette source mesure sur la même échelle, ce qui le place dans la moitié la moins chère de ce groupe.
Sur la même échelle, le pays se situe entre Portugal à 85 et Espagne à 90,7. C'est le voisinage réel que recouvre un rang de 18 sur 39.
Directement comparable à 38 autres pays mesurés sur la même échelle.

Un niveau des prix n'est pas un budget. Il compare un panier normalisé entre pays et ignore ce que vous gagnez, l'écart entre la capitale et une petite ville, et ce qu'un nouvel arrivant paie de loyer par rapport à un locataire en place. À lire comme un point de départ pour comparer et non comme un chiffre sur lequel bâtir un plan.

cells: Niveau des prix de l'ensemble de l'économie
Niveau des prix de l'ensemble de l'économie

faq.q: le Japon : la vie y est-elle chère ?
faq.a: Rapporté à la référence de ce chiffre, le niveau des prix est de 89 pour 2024. C'est tout ce que cette page peut dire honnêtement, car un niveau des prix décrit un panier et non votre vie.

faq.q: De quelle année vient ce chiffre ?
faq.a: C'est la valeur relevée pour 2024. Les statistiques de niveau des prix sont annuelles et arrivent toujours avec du retard : c'est donc la dernière publiée et non un chiffre d'aujourd'hui.

faq.q: Puis-je comparer avec un autre pays ?
faq.a: Seulement avec des pays mesurés sur la même échelle. Cette valeur est donnée en indice, moyenne UE = 100, et un pays situé sur l'autre échelle ne s'y compare pas sans une conversion que personne n'a mesurée.

pages.title: Koszty życia w Szwajcarii: co naprawdę mówi poziom cen
pages.description: Szwajcaria: ile kosztuje tam życie, zmierzone a nie oszacowane: poziom cen wynosi 184,3 za rok 2024, z podziałem na kategorie i źródłem przy każdej liczbie.
paragraphs: Szwajcaria ma poziom cen 184,3, gdy średnia Unii Europejskiej wynosi 100, pomiar za rok 2024. Koszyk zakupów kosztuje tam około 84 procent więcej niż ten sam koszyk w całej Unii.
Dla tego kraju publikowanych jest dwanaście kategorii wydatków, więc podział poniżej jest zmierzony, a nie wyprowadzony z liczby ogólnej.
Wewnątrz koszyka rozpiętość jest większa, niż sugeruje liczba ogólna. Najdroższa kategoria to Edukacja z wynikiem 269,9, najtańsza to Transport z wynikiem 126,9.
Szwajcaria: ceny wzrosły o 0,1 procent w roku do 2024, więc liczby powyżej zdążyły się nieco przesunąć od chwili pomiaru.
Szwajcaria zajmuje miejsce 39 wśród 39 krajów mierzonych przez to źródło w tej samej skali, czyli w droższej połowie tej grupy.
Nic zmierzonego na tej skali nie jest droższe. Poprzednie państwo to Islandia z wynikiem 172,7, spośród 39 mierzonych tak samo.
Bezpośrednio porównywalne z 38 innymi krajami mierzonymi w tej samej skali.

Poziom cen to nie budżet. Porównuje ustandaryzowany koszyk między krajami i nic nie wie o tym, ile zarabiasz, jak daleko stolicy do małego miasta ani ile za wynajem płaci ktoś, kto właśnie przyjechał, wobec kogoś, kto mieszka tam od lat. Czytaj to jako punkt wyjścia do porównania, a nie jako liczbę, na której da się oprzeć plan.

faq.q: Szwajcaria: czy życie jest tam drogie?
faq.a: Wobec punktu odniesienia tej liczby poziom cen wynosi 184,3 za rok 2024. Tyle ta strona może powiedzieć uczciwie, bo poziom cen opisuje koszyk, a nie twoje życie.

faq.q: Z którego roku jest ta liczba?
faq.a: To wartość zebrana za rok 2024. Statystyki poziomu cen są roczne i zawsze przychodzą z opóźnieniem, więc to ostatnia opublikowana wartość, a nie liczba na dziś.

faq.q: Czy mogę to porównać z innym krajem?
faq.a: Tylko z krajami mierzonymi w tej samej skali. Ta wartość podana jest w jednostce indeks, średnia UE = 100, a kraj z drugiej skali nie porównuje się z nią bez przeliczenia, którego nikt nie zmierzył.
